title: Use the optional feature kind: feedback-loop only for producer->consumer correction loops

facts.note: Planner is authoring or editing a feature artifact.
Feature file created or modified (any edit, including behaviour edits that leave `kind:` unchanged).

values: resulting feature has an explicit `kind:` field present (any value, newly added, changed, or unchanged)
facts.note: Content-level observer that reports whether the feature being authored/edited explicitly carries a `kind:` field. Activation is presence-based, not diff-on-kind based: a feature already marked `kind:` is in scope whenever it is edited, even if `kind:` itself is not touched. Whether the feature is actually a correction loop (detect+emit, receive+react, predicate no longer fires) is NOT an activation fact; it is LLM-judged after activation as part of checking compliance, so explicitly marked non-loops are also checked.

fires: A planner writes a new feature that explicitly includes a `kind:` field (any value).
A planner adds or changes the `kind:` value on an existing feature.
A planner edits the behaviour (detection, emission, consumer reaction, acceptances) of a feature that already carries an explicit `kind:` field, even though `kind:` itself is unchanged.
A feature explicitly marked `kind: feedback-loop` whose behaviour is not actually a correction loop is authored or edited — it must still be checked (and flagged).
doesNotFire: A feature, new or existing, that has no `kind:` field after the edit — it defaults to producer-only, the field is optional, and kind validators do not activate, whether or not its behaviour is a loop.

given: You are authoring or editing a feature that carries (or will carry) an explicit optional `kind:` field, which classifies the feature's system archetype — including edits to the behaviour of an already-marked feature where `kind:` itself stays unchanged.
when: You save the feature with an explicit `kind:` present.
then: The explicit `kind:` must be `kind: feedback-loop`, and the feature's behaviour must be a producer->consumer correction loop: a producer detects a condition and emits, a consumer receives and reacts, and the detecting predicate then no longer fires.
prefer: Write exactly `kind: feedback-loop` — the only valid explicit value of feature_kind.
Leave `kind:` absent for any feature that is not a correction loop; absence means producer-only and no kind validator activates.
When editing an already-marked feedback-loop feature, re-check that the edited behaviour still closes the loop (detect+emit, receive+react, predicate no longer fires).
avoid: Marking a producer-only feature (no consumer reaction closing the loop) as `kind: feedback-loop`.
Writing any explicit `kind:` value other than `feedback-loop` (including `producer-only`, which is the default when the field is absent rather than a listed valid value).
Skipping the check because you edited behaviour but not the `kind:` line of an already-marked feature.
why: Feature kind classifies the system archetype; validators activate only for explicitly-marked kinds, so the optional field lets marked loops be validated while existing (unmarked) features are unaffected.
evidence: Every feature with an explicit `kind:` (after any create or edit) has the value `feedback-loop`, and its behaviour is a detect+emit / receive+react / predicate-no-longer-fires loop (judged for every explicitly marked feature, including incorrectly marked non-loops).
Features without `kind:` are treated as producer-only and are not flagged by kind validators.
verifier_detail: Term feature_kind = the feature's system archetype; valid_values: [feedback-loop]; default when absent: producer-only.

Field is optional; validators activate only for explicitly-marked kinds (presence of `kind:` in the feature, regardless of whether the current diff touched it), so features without `kind:` must not be flagged and existing features are unaffected (issue #825).
